issues.t: Lurches or bucks when braking to a stop
issues.sym: While slowing for a light at around 25-35 mph, the SUV suddenly jerks forward and back a few times even though your foot is on the brake. It happens now and then, not on every stop.
issues.why: Owners and dealers point to how the hybrid system's software blends the engine shutting off, the electric motor and the automatic transmission at low speed. Some dealers have called it a known issue and reprogrammed the system, though at least one owner said it came back.
issues.next: Note when it happens (speed, temperature, how hard you were braking) and report it to a Lexus dealer while under warranty. Ask them to check for the latest hybrid and transmission software updates.

issues.t: Hybrid warning messages with rough running and low power
issues.sym: Warning messages telling you to see a dealer scroll across the screens and the Lexus app. The SUV runs rough from a stop up to about 20 mph and may not go faster than about 55 mph, losing power on hills.
issues.why: The SUV has gone into a protective reduced-power mode after the hybrid or transmission computers logged faults. In reported cases the dealer cleared codes without finding one clear cause; low 12-volt battery voltage and software errors were both suspected.
issues.next: Drive gently to a Lexus dealer, or have it towed if power is very limited. Ask them to save the trouble codes and check for software updates and the 12-volt battery before clearing anything, so there is a record if it comes back.

issues.t: Check engine light with cam timing code P05CE00
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, often after a cold start, with no change in how the SUV drives. A scan tool shows code P05CE00 (cold start camshaft timing, bank 1).
issues.why: A locking pin in the exhaust variable valve timing unit can stick for a moment, and an error in the engine computer's programming makes it flag that as a fault. Lexus changed the engine computer logic to fix it.
issues.next: Have a Lexus dealer confirm the code and apply the engine computer update from the service bulletin. It is covered under warranty.

issues.t: Clicking from front axles when turning and accelerating
issues.sym: A rhythmic clicking from one or both front wheels when you accelerate while turning, like pulling out of a parking spot. There may be no grease leaking from the axle boots.
issues.why: Lexus found a problem with the front drive shafts on some early TX 350s and released an updated drive shaft assembly.
issues.next: Tell the dealer exactly when the click happens. If it matches the bulletin, the front drive shaft is replaced with the updated part under warranty.

issues.t: Sunroof creaks and dash or headliner rattles
issues.sym: Creaking from the panoramic moonroof, squeaks from the dashboard, or rattles from the headliner or a rear door panel, often changing with temperature or road surface.
issues.why: Owners report loose-fitting headliner and trim pieces and moonroof rails or frames that flex. Some needed several dealer visits, and in one case the moonroof rail and frame were replaced.
issues.next: Record a short video with sound and show the dealer where the noise comes from. Keep copies of every repair order in case the problem keeps coming back.

issues.t: Mark Levinson audio cuts out or lacks bass
issues.sym: With the Mark Levinson stereo, sound cuts out at high volume with heavy bass settings, or the bass sounds thin and the rear speakers and subwoofer seem weak or silent.
issues.why: Lexus changed the sound system's amplifier to fix these problems on 2024-2025 TX models with the Mark Levinson system.
issues.next: Ask a Lexus dealer to check the system against the service bulletin. If it matches, the updated amplifier is installed under warranty.

issues.sym: You press the fuel door release button and the fuel door stays shut, so you can't refuel.
issues.why: Lexus issued a service bulletin for TX models where the fuel lid fails to open when the release is pressed; owners report dealers replacing the fuel door parts.
issues.next: Try the release again with the SUV unlocked. If it still won't open, have a Lexus dealer repair it under the bulletin rather than prying on the door, which can damage the paint.

issues.t: Touchscreen glitches, stuck day or night mode, or passcode prompts
issues.sym: The center screen stays stuck in day or night brightness, starts slowly, or now and then refuses to start until you enter a 6-digit passcode. Voice commands, profiles or navigation can act up too.
issues.why: These are software issues in the Lexus multimedia system. Lexus released head unit software updates and a bulletin for the stuck day/night mode. The passcode prompt is tied to the Lexus account PIN setting.
issues.next: Make sure the multimedia software is up to date (ask the dealer at your next visit). For passcode prompts, check the PIN setting under Account and Security Settings in the Lexus app.

issues.t: Side curtain airbags may not deploy correctly (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. In a side crash or rollover, the curtain airbags could unroll the wrong way and partly come out through an open window.
issues.why: The driver and passenger curtain airbags may not unfold as designed, so they don't meet the federal ejection-protection standard.
issues.next: Check your VIN on the Lexus or NHTSA recall site. The dealer replaces both curtain airbags for free.

issues.t: Gauge cluster may not show speed or warning lights (recall)
issues.sym: When you start the SUV, the instrument panel may not show your speed or the brake and tire pressure warning lights.
issues.why: A software error during startup can stop the instrument panel from displaying these items.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Non-plug-in models get a free over-the-air software update; the TX 550h+ goes to the dealer, who updates or replaces the panel for free.

issues.t: Rearview camera image may not appear (recall)
issues.sym: When you shift into reverse, the backup camera picture may not show up on the screen.
issues.why: A camera software problem can stop the rearview image from displaying, which breaks the federal rear-visibility rule.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and use mirrors and look over your shoulder until it's fixed. The dealer updates the camera software or replaces the camera for free.

issues.t: Backup camera can freeze or go blank (recall)
issues.sym: On SUVs with the 360-degree Panoramic View Monitor, the backup image can freeze or the screen can go blank in reverse.
issues.why: A software error in the parking assist computer that runs the camera system.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer updates the parking assist software for free.

issues.t: Load capacity label shows the wrong weight (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. The tire and loading label in the door jamb lists the wrong added-weight numbers.
issues.why: The label was printed with inaccurate load figures, so it doesn't meet the federal tire-and-rim labeling rule. Overloading based on it could strain the tires.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the label for free; until then, don't load the SUV to its limit.

issues.sym: Usually no warning. If the part fails, the rear of the SUV can suddenly feel loose or unstable and you could lose control.
issues.why: Some rear axle carriers (the part holding the rear wheel hub) were made with too little material strength and can break.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls right away. The dealer checks the part code and replaces the rear axle carriers for free if needed.

issues.sym: Usually no warning before a failure. A cracked knuckle could make the steering feel odd or cause a sudden loss of steering control.
issues.why: A manufacturing error may leave the front steering knuckles (the parts that hold the front wheels and connect to the steering) prone to cracking.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get it inspected promptly. The dealer inspects and replaces the front knuckles for free as needed.

issues.t: Pulls or drifts to one side
issues.sym: The SUV slowly drifts left or right on a straight, flat road, and you have to hold the wheel slightly off center.
issues.why: Lexus mounts the tires as matched sets at the factory to limit pull; alignment or a mismatched tire can still cause drift. Owners have also reported alignment problems on new TXs.
issues.next: Check that all four tire pressures match the door label. If it still pulls, ask the dealer to check alignment and tire placement under warranty.

issues.sym: After the SUV sits for a while, it is slow to start or won't start, or you see odd warnings caused by low voltage.
issues.why: Lexus bulletins warn that storage time, heat or cold, and the small power draw from the SUV's electronics can drain and shorten the life of the 12-volt battery.
issues.next: If the SUV will sit for more than a couple of weeks, drive it regularly or use a battery maintainer. Have the dealer test the battery if you get repeated low-voltage warnings.

issues.t: Driver floor mat slides out of its clips
issues.sym: The driver's floor mat moves forward or bunches up under the pedals.
issues.why: The mat must be hooked onto its retaining clips. Lexus issued a bulletin about these clips on 2024 models; a loose mat can get in the way of the pedals.
issues.next: Make sure the mat is the correct one for the TX and clipped onto both hooks. Never stack a second mat on top. Ask the dealer to check the clips if they won't hold.
